chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Aswad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

"No one may observe a waiting period (iddah) for more than three [months], except a woman for her husband, until her waiting period expires." Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: "Regarding what the preceding hadiths included, that the widow does not spend the night away from her house, this is understood as being recommended (istihbab) and preferable. And if she spent the night elsewhere, there is no harm in that, according to what the later hadiths included. And to clarify this further is what has been narrated:"

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَاب: Recommended (a level of legal ruling below obligation)
key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: The one whose husband has died (widow)

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum duration for a widow's waiting period and is she required to stay in her husband's house?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the general rule that the waiting period (iddah) for any deceased spouse is limited to three months, distinguishing it from the longer period prescribed for pregnant women. Shaykh al-Tusi’s commentary, citing Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, clarifies that while staying in the marital home is highly recommended (istihbab) for the widow, it is not strictly obligatory, a nuance harmonized with other hadiths that permit staying elsewhere without fault.
